# BMW Product Management Challenge: Assignment Specification & Requirements Guide

**Challenge:** AI for Product Decision Making  
**Host:** BMW Group Product Management  
**Scope Focus:** Automotive Product Development Process — Steps 1 & 2 (Market Research & Product Planning to Gate G1 Concept Freeze)  
**Target Derivatives:** BMW 1 Series (F70), BMW 5 Series (G60/G68), BMW 7 Series (G70), and Future Successor Lines (Neue Klasse Architecture)  
**Target Markets:** Europe (EU), United States (US), China (CN), and Rest of World (RoW)  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Mission Statement

Modern automotive product management requires synthesizing billions of fragmented market signals, customer reviews, warranty reports, competitor actions, and strategic corporate roadmaps into a coherent, customer-facing product specification. Today, this process spans approximately **two years** per vehicle generation and is predominantly manual, fragmented, and vulnerable to subjective bias.

### The Mission
Develop an AI-powered, human-in-the-loop enterprise application that:
1. **Ingests Heterogeneous Data**: Combines internal BMW customer feedback, quantitative satisfaction surveys, vehicle equipment catalogs, and strategic corporate reports.
2. **Extracts Actionable Signals**: Discovers recurring complaints, unmet customer needs, competitor advantages, and emerging market trends, each strictly linked to originating evidence.
3. **Derives SMART Product Requirements**: Formulates clear, customer-facing, realistic, and measurable requirements adhering to SMART criteria.
4. **Prioritizes with Explainable Logic**: Applies an objective, transparent, multi-factor scoring methodology that balances customer value, regional volume impact, corporate strategy, and implementation complexity.
5. **Keeps the Product Manager Firmly in the Loop**: Enables the PM to review, approve, reject, modify, or challenge requirements, rationales, and underlying evidence.
6. **Maintains a Forensic Audit Trail**: Chronologically logs every system derivation, PM intervention, score override, and decision rationale to guarantee end-to-end governance.

---

## 2. Automotive Product Development Process Alignment

BMW management explicitly bounded the scope of this challenge to **Steps 1 and 2** of the 13-stage Automotive Product Development Lifecycle:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Step1["Step 1: Market Research & Needs Analysis"]
        A1["Activities: Market Research, Customer Insights, Competitor Benchmarking, Trend Analysis"]
        A2["Deliverables: Market Opportunity Report, Customer Needs Document, Target Segments"]
        G0["Decision Gate: G0 — Project Approval"]
        A1 --> A2 --> G0
    end

    subgraph Step2["Step 2: Product Planning (Core App Focus)"]
        B1["Activities: Define Product Vision, Positioning, SMART Feature Prioritization, Trade-off Resolution"]
        B2["Deliverables: Product Plan, Project Charter, Prioritized Requirement List, Initial Business Sizing"]
        G1["Decision Gate: G1 — Concept Freeze"]
        B1 --> B2 --> G1
    end

    subgraph Step3["Steps 3 to 13: Concept to Continuous Feedback"]
        C1["G2 Feasibility -> G3 Design Freeze -> ... -> G9 SOP -> Step 13 Market Feedback Loop"]
    end

    Step1 --> Step2 --> Step3

    classDef default fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,color:#000000,stroke-width:1px;
    style Step1 fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000
    style Step2 fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000
    style Step3 fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000
```

### Boundary Definitions
* **In-Scope (Customer-Facing Product Attributes)**:
  * Interior comfort, ergonomics, and spatial packaging
  * Infotainment, operating system UX, and connected digital services
  * Climatization and thermal comfort controls
  * Driving experience and dynamic perception
  * Real-world charging UX and range perception
  * Equipment packaging, option bundling, and regional variant differentiation
* **Out-of-Scope**:
  * Regulatory and homologation compliance (e.g., UNECE safety, emissions type approval)
  * Low-level component specifications and supplier engineering schematics
  * Detailed unit economics, factory tooling capex, and bill-of-materials pricing calculations (rough implementation complexity/effort sizing is utilized as a prioritization factor)

---

## 3. Data Ecosystem & Inputs Profile

The application processes four distinct tiers of heterogeneous data:

```
BMW-Data/
├── F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx              # 4,076 rows (1 Series - UK, JP, SE, FR)
├── G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx              # 5,005 rows (5 Series - US, KR, GB, JP, SE)
├── G70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx              # 4,690 rows (7 Series - US, KR, JP, GB, CA)
├── F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx    # Quantitative satisfaction studies (China, EU, US)
├── sales_volumes.xlsx                       # Market deliveries (2024, 2025, 2030 projections)
├── F70_OptionList.PDF                       # Official German equipment catalog & packaging (1er)
├── G60_OptionList.PDF                       # Official German equipment catalog & packaging (5er)
├── G70_OptionList.PDF                       # Official German equipment catalog & packaging (7er)
└── BMW_Group_Report_2025.pdf / Q-Deck       # 400-page strategic corporate & financial report
```

### Dataset Characteristics

| Dataset | Volume | Key Attributes | Strategic Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Customer Feedback** | 13,771 rows | `ID`, `Country`, `Engine Type` (ICE, BEV, PHEV), `Feedback Type` (Likes, DTU, Defect, Wants), `Customer Feedback`, `Vfc Category` | Voice of the customer; ground-truth operational friction, ergonomics, and feature desires. |
| **Customer Studies** | Quantitative sheets | Likert ratings (US) & Mean satisfaction scores (CN vs. EU) across 15 vehicle systems | Macro-level customer satisfaction benchmarks; correlates qualitative text with quantitative validation. |
| **Sales Volumes** | 4 regions $\times$ 3 vehicle lines | Volumes for 2024, 2025, and 2030 projections across EU, US, China, and RoW | Objective volume weighting factor for prioritization formulas. |
| **Option Catalogs** | 3 German PDFs | Standard vs. optional equipment, option codes, bundle packages (Innovation, Travel, Comfort) | Grounds proposed requirements in realistic production packaging. |
| **Strategic Report Deck** | ~400 pages | Neue Klasse platform roadmap, R&D priorities, BEV delivery targets, digital software KPIs | Strategic validation layer; ties customer desires to BMW engineering investments. |

---

## 4. Evaluation Criteria & Scoring Rubric

The challenge will be judged on five primary criteria, with one critical guiding principle:

| Dimension | Weight | Key Evaluation Requirements |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Decision & Scoring Logic** | 25% | Quality, consistency, and mathematical explainability of prioritization. Clear demonstration of how evidence sources are weighted and combined, and how trade-offs and conflicting signals are resolved. |
| **Workflow & Human Decision-Making** | 20% | Completeness of the end-to-end workflow from raw findings to prioritized requirements. Clearly defined roles, decision gates, and boundaries between autonomous AI and mandatory human review. |
| **Traceability & Auditability** | 20% | Full backward lineage from every requirement and score back to originating quotes, surveys, and report slides. Complete, chronological, tamper-evident audit history of all approvals, edits, and rejections. |
| **Solution Quality, Usability & Feasibility** | 20% | Prototype UI/UX polish, usability for BMW Product Managers and engineering peers, realistic applicability in an enterprise automotive environment, and quality of SMART formulations. |
| **Innovation, Scalability & Business Impact** | 15% | Originality of approach, cross-derivative scalability (F70 $\to$ G60 $\to$ G70 $\to$ Neue Klasse), reduction in manual requirement definition cycle time, and prevention of costly late-stage engineering rework. |

### The Winning Differentiator: "We Reward Honesty"
> **Direct Quote from BMW Challenge Evaluation Criteria:**  
> *"We reward honesty. Trustworthy AI acknowledges uncertainty. Show us where your app lacks evidence, encounters conflicting signals, or reaches uncertain conclusions, and how this is surfaced to the PM. Honest limitations are a strength, not a weakness."*

The application must include an explicit **Uncertainty & Evidence Confidence Index** that transparently highlights:
1. Low sample size / weak empirical support
2. Regional contradictions (e.g., EU Autobahn driver desires vs. China chauffeur comfort)
3. Extrapolations based on forward-looking assumptions (e.g., 2030 battery/software tech) versus proven historical data

---

## 5. SMART Requirements Framework

BMW requirements must strictly comply with the **SMART** standard:

| SMART Dimension | Definition | Automotive Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Specific** | Concrete and unambiguous system or feature scope | Exact UI component, sensor, or interior system |
| **Measurable** | Objective engineering/UX KPIs & thresholds | Clear quantifiable metrics (e.g. latency $< 45\text{ms}$, 60 fps) |
| **Attainable** | Feasible within vehicle architecture & manufacturing | Compatible with platform packaging & wiring harness |
| **Relevant** | Meaningfully solves verified customer pain | Directly resolves top complaint or aligns with brand strategy |
| **Timely** | Explicit SOP target & vehicle milestone | SOP 2028 (LCI / Successor / Neue Klasse milestone) |

### Benchmark Example: From Complaint to SMART Requirement
* **Raw Voice of Customer (`G70-0891`)**: *"Customer noted she would have chosen the Home theater screen, but it obstructs the view out the rear and BMW does not offer a camera/rear-view mirror screen."*
* **Unacceptable Requirement (Vague)**: *"Improve rear visibility when the theater screen is down."*
* **SMART Requirement (`REQ-G70-VIS-001`)**:
  * **Specific**: Full-display digital streaming rear-view mirror system utilizing an aerodynamic roof-mounted wide-angle camera feeding directly into the central rear-view mirror.
  * **Measurable**: End-to-end video latency $< 45\text{ ms}$; frame rate $\ge 60\text{ fps}$ at $1080\text{p}$; dynamic range $> 120\text{ dB}$ (headlight anti-glare); camera lens auto-defrosting and wash nozzle operational from $-30^\circ\text{C}$ to $+65^\circ\text{C}$.
  * **Attainable**: Integrates with the existing Neue Klasse roof shark-fin camera housing and high-speed automotive Ethernet backbone.
  * **Relevant**: Eliminates the #1 safety blocker preventing theater screen adoption; projected to increase Theater Screen package take-rate by 18%.
  * **Timely**: Targeted for SOP 2028 (G70 LCI / Neue Klasse Luxury derivative).
  * **Package Strategy**: Standard on i7 M70; optional in Innovation Package for base derivatives.

---

## 6. Key Mentors & Stakeholder Insights

1. **Bene_BMW (Product Management Pain Points)**:
   * *Cross-Market Regional Balancing*: Preferences differ radically by climate, usage habits, and culture. A single global specification often fails in either Europe, the US, or China.
   * *Predecessor Feedback Cycles*: Capturing field insights from outgoing models (e.g., F70, G60, G70) and projecting them 3–5 years ahead into future vehicle architectures.
   * *2-Year Timeline*: Requirement prioritization is not a one-time script; it is a collaborative, iterative governance process over ~24 months.
2. **ThomasFremuthBMW**:
   * Ground proposals in real evidence; maintain strict data hygiene (do not commit raw internal data to public repositories).
3. **Sebastian_BMW & ThomasBMW**:
   * Scope is tightly focused on Steps 1 & 2 of the automotive development framework.

---

## 7. Expected Deliverables

### 7.1 BMW-Provided Deliverable Wording

The following four expected deliverables are reproduced from the BMW wording supplied to the team.

#### 1. Concept and Demonstrable Prototype

> A concept and demonstrable prototype of an AI-powered product requirements application that processes heterogeneous inputs, derives product requirements, supports prioritization, and integrates human review.

#### 2. Structured Sample Requirements List

> A structured sample list of derived product requirements. Each requirement should include a unique identifier, a clear and actionable description, its linked findings and sources, a priority or score, the applied prioritization rationale, an evidence level, the key future-facing assumptions and uncertainties and its current decision status.

#### 3. End-to-End Workflow

> A clearly defined end-to-end workflow showing how inputs are processed into proposed and prioritized requirements, which activities the AI performs autonomously, and where human review is mandatory.

#### 4. Demonstrable Audit Trail

> A demonstrable audit trail that makes each requirement traceable from its underlying findings and sources through consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decision-making. It should record relevant changes to requirement content, scores, priorities, evidence, and status, including who or what initiated each change, when it occurred, and the documented rationale.

### 7.2 Delivery Checklist

- [ ] **Concept & Working Application Prototype**: Explain the concept and demonstrate heterogeneous input processing, derived product requirements, prioritization, and integrated human review.
- [ ] **Structured Sample Requirements List**: Include a unique identifier, clear and actionable description, linked findings and sources, priority or score, applied prioritization rationale, evidence level, key future-facing assumptions and uncertainties, and current decision status for every requirement.
- [ ] **End-to-End Workflow Definition**: Show how inputs become proposed and prioritized requirements, which activities the AI performs autonomously, and where human review is mandatory.
- [ ] **Traceable & Reconstructable Audit Trail**: Trace requirements from findings and sources through consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decisions. Record relevant content, score, priority, evidence, and status changes with initiator, timestamp, and rationale.

### 7.3 Presentation Deliverable

- [ ] **Pitch Presentation Deck (3–5 min)**: Compelling narrative demonstrating real-world value, data grounding, and Trustworthy AI principles.

See `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the concrete prototype features, artifact formats, implementation responsibilities, and acceptance criteria mapped to these deliverables.

Creating `.env` alone does not implement those missing readers.
10: 
11: ## Variables and Consumers
12: 
13: | Variable | Template default | Consumer / purpose |
14: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
15: | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Empty; fill privately | Role 2's backend model adapter; required for live calls |
16: | `OPENAI_MODEL` | `gpt-4o-mini` | Model adapter; selected model recorded in run provenance |
17: | `BMW_RAW_DATA_DIR` | `./BMW-Data` | Role 1 raw XLSX/PDF conversion |
18: | `BMW_DATA_DIR` | `./var/processed` | Converter output and existing processed-input loader |
19: | `BMW_OUTPUT_DIR` | `./var/exports` | Role 3 sample/audit/freeze exports; Role 5 private delivery artifacts |
20: | `BMW_CACHE_DIR` | `./var/cache` | Role 2 private model/retrieval cache |
21: | `NEO4J_URI` | `bolt://localhost:7687` | Backend/data graph connection |
22: | `NEO4J_USER` | `neo4j` | Graph authentication; shared with Compose initialization |
23: | `NEO4J_PASSWORD` | `bmwpassword` | Existing local development password; shared with Compose |
24: | `API_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Backend listen address, not a UI destination |
25: | `API_PORT` | `8000` | Backend listen/published port |
26: | `API_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:${API_PORT}` | Frontend API origin; dotenv resolves the port reference |
27: | `STREAMLIT_SERVER_ADDRESS` | `0.0.0.0` | Streamlit listen address |
28: | `STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT` | `8501` | Streamlit listen/published port |
29: 
30: Weights, evidence thresholds, forecast/reference policy, allowed statuses and tool budgets belong to versioned application policy, not duplicate per-developer environment knobs. Actual source values are read from imported data.
31: 
32: ## Local Setup
33: 
34: 1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` at the repository root.
35: 2. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the processes performing live AI calls. Frontend-only work can leave it empty and connect to a team backend through `API_BASE_URL`.
36: 3. Put the supplied inputs in `BMW_RAW_DATA_DIR`; conversion produces files under `BMW_DATA_DIR`.
37: 4. The launcher starts the backend and UI using these settings; jobs/exporters use the same root-resolved paths.
38: 
39: Root `config.py` must explicitly load the root `.env` with process-environment precedence (`override=False`). Resolve relative paths against the repository root, never a caller's current directory. Parse/validate ports and URLs centrally; require OpenAI credentials at the live-model boundary rather than breaking unrelated UI/fixture imports.
40: 
41: Do not load a separate `.env` from `pipeline/`, `services/`, or `ui/`. The loader may run once in each process; application modules import the resulting settings. Never include the key/password in diagnostic output.
42: 
43: ## Container Wiring — Same Names, Different Network
44: 
45: Owner 3 adapts the existing Compose file using the root `.env`:
46: 
47: - API receives `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, Neo4j credentials, and data/output/cache settings. It connects to `NEO4J_URI=bolt://neo4j:7687` inside Compose.
48: - Neo4j initialization uses the same `NEO4J_USER`/`NEO4J_PASSWORD`; no second hard-coded credential declaration.
49: - UI receives `API_BASE_URL=http://api:${API_PORT}` plus native Streamlit server settings. It does not receive OpenAI credentials.
50: - Backend/Streamlit commands and published ports use the canonical values instead of conflicting hard-coded CLI overrides.
51: - Raw/processed/export/cache paths are mounted and overridden to the corresponding container paths using these same variable names. Raw files may be read-only; conversion/export/cache directories must be writable by their owning processes.
52: - Streamlit reads native server environment before its CLI initializes. The local launcher must export `STREAMLIT_SERVER_*` before starting it; loading dotenv only inside the already-running UI script is too late for custom server ports.
53: 
54: Compose service-host overrides describe container topology. They are not new configuration aliases or a second team env file. An API URL may intentionally point to a remote/shared backend, independently of the local backend bind address.
55: 
56: ## Role Ownership
57: 
58: - **Role 1:** consumes raw/processed settings through config; supplies converter/manifest behavior.
59: - **Role 2:** consumes OpenAI/model/cache settings through config; removes legacy provider fallback/imports with Role 3.
60: - **Role 3:** owns the template, root config reader, startup validation, runner, Compose and environment integration tests. Changes to variable names go through this owner.
61: - **Role 4:** consumes API settings through the shared reader/client; renders UI and uses native Streamlit startup settings. No model keys or direct graph connection.
62: - **Role 5:** uses delivered export/presentation locations and startup instructions; no separate application settings.
63: 
64: ## Integration Acceptance Checks
65: 
66: 1. Template has one assignment per key and no real API key; `.env` and private outputs are ignored by Git.
67: 2. Root config resolves the template paths from any working directory; process overrides win.
68: 3. Changing `API_PORT` updates the local interpolated API origin unless an explicit remote `API_BASE_URL` is supplied.
69: 4. OpenAI-only configuration produces a live model call after valid credentials are supplied. Empty credentials produce a clear unavailable result, never Anthropic fallback.
70: 5. Native Streamlit address/port apply before server startup; UI connects locally and through the Compose service name.
71: 6. Compose graph credentials match backend settings, and input/output/cache mounts have the intended read/write access.
72: 7. All pipeline/API/UI modules import canonical settings; no `load_dotenv` or duplicated `os.getenv`/defaults appears outside the config/launcher boundary.

(End of file - total 72 lines)

Weights, evidence thresholds, forecast/reference policy, allowed statuses and tool budgets belong to versioned application policy, not duplicate per-developer environment knobs. Actual source values are read from imported data.

## Local Setup

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` at the repository root.
2. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the processes performing live AI calls. Frontend-only work can leave it empty and connect to a team backend through `API_BASE_URL`.
3. Put the supplied inputs in `BMW_RAW_DATA_DIR`; conversion produces files under `BMW_DATA_DIR`.
4. The launcher starts the backend and UI using these settings; jobs/exporters use the same root-resolved paths.

Root `config.py` must explicitly load the root `.env` with process-environment precedence (`override=False`). Resolve relative paths against the repository root, never a caller's current directory. Parse/validate ports and URLs centrally; require OpenAI credentials at the live-model boundary rather than breaking unrelated UI/fixture imports.

Do not load a separate `.env` from `pipeline/`, `services/`, or `ui/`. The loader may run once in each process; application modules import the resulting settings. Never include the key/password in diagnostic output.

## Container Wiring — Same Names, Different Network

Owner 3 adapts the existing Compose file using the root `.env`:

- API receives `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, Neo4j credentials, and data/output/cache settings. It connects to `NEO4J_URI=bolt://neo4j:7687` inside Compose.
- Neo4j initialization uses the same `NEO4J_USER`/`NEO4J_PASSWORD`; no second hard-coded credential declaration.
- UI receives `API_BASE_URL=http://api:${API_PORT}` plus native Streamlit server settings. It does not receive OpenAI credentials.
- Backend/Streamlit commands and published ports use the canonical values instead of conflicting hard-coded CLI overrides.
- Raw/processed/export/cache paths are mounted and overridden to the corresponding container paths using these same variable names. Raw files may be read-only; conversion/export/cache directories must be writable by their owning processes.
- Streamlit reads native server environment before its CLI initializes. The local launcher must export `STREAMLIT_SERVER_*` before starting it; loading dotenv only inside the already-running UI script is too late for custom server ports.

Compose service-host overrides describe container topology. They are not new configuration aliases or a second team env file. An API URL may intentionally point to a remote/shared backend, independently of the local backend bind address.

## Role Ownership

- **Role 1:** consumes raw/processed settings through config; supplies converter/manifest behavior.
- **Role 2:** consumes OpenAI/model/cache settings through config; removes legacy provider fallback/imports with Role 3.
- **Role 3:** owns the template, root config reader, startup validation, runner, Compose and environment integration tests. Changes to variable names go through this owner.
- **Role 4:** consumes API settings through the shared reader/client; renders UI and uses native Streamlit startup settings. No model keys or direct graph connection.
- **Role 5:** uses delivered export/presentation locations and startup instructions; no separate application settings.

## Integration Acceptance Checks

1. Template has one assignment per key and no real API key; `.env` and private outputs are ignored by Git.
2. Root config resolves the template paths from any working directory; process overrides win.
3. Changing `API_PORT` updates the local interpolated API origin unless an explicit remote `API_BASE_URL` is supplied.
4. OpenAI-only configuration produces a live model call after valid credentials are supplied. Empty credentials produce a clear unavailable result, never Anthropic fallback.
5. Native Streamlit address/port apply before server startup; UI connects locally and through the Compose service name.
6. Compose graph credentials match backend settings, and input/output/cache mounts have the intended read/write access.
7. All pipeline/API/UI modules import canonical settings; no `load_dotenv` or duplicated `os.getenv`/defaults appears outside the config/launcher boundary.

"""
Step 04 — Extract signals from feedback using LLM API (OpenAI / Anthropic).

For each (model, vfc2) combination with sufficient feedback,
the LLM extracts a structured Signal: sentiment, intensity, key themes,
verbatim samples, and flags conflicting source channels.

API call budget: ~1 call per 10 VFC batches.

Run: python pipeline/04_extract_signals.py
"""
import json
import sys
import time
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
from config import (
    NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD,
    OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL,
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_MODEL,
    LLM_PROVIDER, EVIDENCE_TIERS, SOURCE_CHANNEL_BIAS,
)
from neo4j import GraphDatabase

if LLM_PROVIDER == "openai":
    import openai as llm_client_lib
else:
    import anthropic as llm_client_lib

BATCH_SIZE = 10   # VFC groups per API call
MIN_FEEDBACKS = 3  # minimum to generate a signal


SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a BMW product intelligence analyst. Your task is to extract structured signals from customer feedback grouped by VFC (Vehicle Function Category) tag.

For each VFC group you will receive:
- model: the BMW model code (F70=1 Series, G60=5 Series, G70=7 Series)
- vfc2: the VFC Level 2 category
- feedbacks: list of customer feedback texts with their source channel type

Output a JSON array — one object per VFC group — with this exact schema:
{
  "model": "F70",
  "vfc2": "INFOTAINMENT",
  "sentiment": "negative",          // "positive", "negative", or "neutral"
  "intensity": 7.5,                 // 0-10, how strong the signal is
  "key_themes": ["slow response", "outdated UI"],
  "verbatim_samples": ["exact quote 1", "exact quote 2"],  // max 3, verbatim from input
  "has_conflict": false,            // true if source channels disagree significantly
  "conflict_detail": null,          // explain conflict if has_conflict is true
  "data_gaps": [],                  // list gaps: what data would improve this signal
  "ai_inferred_vfc": false          // true if this VFC was AI-inferred (not from original tag)
}

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Never invent data. Base everything strictly on the provided texts.
2. verbatim_samples must be exact quotes from the input, not paraphrases.
3. If source channels clearly disagree (e.g. GENERAL_SURVEY positive, COMPLAINT_CHANNEL negative), set has_conflict=true and describe the conflict.
4. If fewer than 5 feedbacks exist, note this as a data gap: "Only N feedbacks — insufficient for strong signal".
5. sentiment must reflect the MAJORITY signal, not just complaints (COMPLAINT_CHANNEL is biased).
6. data_gaps should list what additional data would be needed to increase confidence."""


def get_driver():
    return GraphDatabase.driver(NEO4J_URI, auth=(NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD))


def load_feedback_by_vfc(session) -> dict:
    """Returns {(model, vfc2): [{"text": ..., "channel": ..., "ftype": ...}]}"""
    result = session.run("""
        MATCH (fb:CustomerFeedback)-[:TAGGED_VFC2]->(v:VFCTag)
        WHERE fb.text IS NOT NULL AND fb.text_length > 20
        RETURN fb.model AS model, v.vfc2 AS vfc2,
               fb.text AS text,
               fb.source_channel_type AS channel,
               fb.feedback_type AS ftype,
               fb.text_quality_confidence AS tqc
        ORDER BY model, vfc2
    """)

    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for row in result:
        key = (row["model"], row["vfc2"])
        groups[key].append({
            "text": row["text"][:500],  # cap length for API
            "channel": row["channel"] or "STANDARD_SURVEY",
            "ftype": row["ftype"] or "unclassified",
            "tqc": row["tqc"] or 0.8,
        })
    return groups


def determine_evidence_tier(count: int) -> str:
    if count >= EVIDENCE_TIERS["STRONG"]["min_feedbacks"]:
        return "STRONG"
    if count >= EVIDENCE_TIERS["MODERATE"]["min_feedbacks"]:
        return "MODERATE"
    return "WEAK"


def call_llm(client, batch: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Send a batch of VFC groups to LLM for signal extraction."""
    user_content = json.dumps(batch, ensure_ascii=False)

    if LLM_PROVIDER == "openai":
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=OPENAI_MODEL,
            max_tokens=4096,
            response_format={"type": "json_object"},
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT + "\n\nReturn a JSON object with key 'signals' containing the array."},
                {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
            ],
        )
        raw = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        parsed = json.loads(raw)
        return parsed.get("signals", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else parsed
    else:
        response = client.messages.create(
            model=CLAUDE_MODEL,
            max_tokens=4096,
            system=[{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM_PROMPT, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_content}],
        )
        raw = response.content[0].text.strip()
        if "```" in raw:
            raw = raw.split("```")[1]
            if raw.startswith("json"):
                raw = raw[4:]
        return json.loads(raw)


def save_signal(session, model: str, vfc2: str, signal: dict, count: int):
    tier = determine_evidence_tier(count)
    sid = hashlib.md5(f"{model}|{vfc2}".encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    signal_id = f"SIG-{model}-{vfc2.replace(' ', '_')[:20]}"

    session.run("""
        MERGE (s:Signal {signal_id: $signal_id})
        SET s.model         = $model,
            s.vfc2          = $vfc2,
            s.sentiment     = $sentiment,
            s.intensity     = $intensity,
            s.key_themes    = $key_themes,
            s.verbatim_samples = $verbatim,
            s.has_conflict  = $has_conflict,
            s.conflict_detail = $conflict_detail,
            s.data_gaps     = $data_gaps,
            s.evidence_tier = $tier,
            s.feedback_count = $count,
            s.ai_inferred_vfc = $ai_inferred
        WITH s
        MATCH (v:VFCTag {vfc2: $vfc2})
        MERGE (s)-[:EVIDENCES]->(v)
    """,
        signal_id=signal_id, model=model, vfc2=vfc2,
        sentiment=signal.get("sentiment", "neutral"),
        intensity=float(signal.get("intensity", 5.0)),
        key_themes=signal.get("key_themes", []),
        verbatim=signal.get("verbatim_samples", []),
        has_conflict=signal.get("has_conflict", False),
        conflict_detail=signal.get("conflict_detail"),
        data_gaps=signal.get("data_gaps", []),
        tier=tier,
        count=count,
        ai_inferred=signal.get("ai_inferred_vfc", False),
    )


def main():
    print("=== Step 04: Extract signals via Claude API ===")

    if LLM_PROVIDER == "openai":
        if not OPENAI_API_KEY:
            print("ERROR: OPENAI_API_KEY not set")
            sys.exit(1)
        client = llm_client_lib.OpenAI(api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY)
        print(f"  Using OpenAI model: {OPENAI_MODEL}")
    else:
        if not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:
            print("ERROR: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set")
            sys.exit(1)
        client = llm_client_lib.Anthropic(api_key=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
        print(f"  Using Anthropic model: {CLAUDE_MODEL}")
    driver = get_driver()

    with driver.session() as session:
        groups = load_feedback_by_vfc(session)
        print(f"  Found {len(groups)} (model, vfc2) groups")

        # Prepare batches
        items = [
            (model, vfc2, feedbacks)
            for (model, vfc2), feedbacks in groups.items()
            if len(feedbacks) >= MIN_FEEDBACKS
        ]
        print(f"  Processing {len(items)} groups (≥{MIN_FEEDBACKS} feedbacks)")

        total_signals = 0
        for batch_start in range(0, len(items), BATCH_SIZE):
            batch_items = items[batch_start: batch_start + BATCH_SIZE]
            batch_payload = [
                {
                    "model": model,
                    "vfc2": vfc2,
                    "feedback_count": len(feedbacks),
                    "feedbacks": [
                        {"text": fb["text"], "channel": fb["channel"], "ftype": fb["ftype"]}
                        for fb in feedbacks[:20]  # cap at 20 per group
                    ],
                }
                for model, vfc2, feedbacks in batch_items
            ]

            print(f"  Batch {batch_start // BATCH_SIZE + 1}: {len(batch_payload)} VFC groups...")
            try:
                signals = call_llm(client, batch_payload)
                for i, (model, vfc2, feedbacks) in enumerate(batch_items):
                    if i < len(signals):
                        save_signal(session, model, vfc2, signals[i], len(feedbacks))
                        total_signals += 1
                time.sleep(0.5)  # rate limit courtesy
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  [ERROR] Batch {batch_start // BATCH_SIZE + 1}: {e}")
                continue

        print(f"  Total signals saved: {total_signals}")

    driver.close()
    print("Done.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT + "\n\nReturn a JSON object with key 'signals' containing the array."},
                {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
            ],
        )
        raw = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        parsed = json.loads(raw)
        return parsed.get("signals", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else parsed
    else:
        response = client.messages.create(
            model=CLAUDE_MODEL,
            max_tokens=4096,
            system=[{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM_PROMPT, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_content}],
        )
        raw = response.content[0].text.strip()
        if "```" in raw:
            raw = raw.split("```")[1]
            if raw.startswith("json"):
                raw = raw[4:]
        return json.loads(raw)


def save_signal(session, model: str, vfc2: str, signal: dict, count: int):
    tier = determine_evidence_tier(count)
    sid = hashlib.md5(f"{model}|{vfc2}".encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    signal_id = f"SIG-{model}-{vfc2.replace(' ', '_')[:20]}"

    session.run("""
        MERGE (s:Signal {signal_id: $signal_id})
        SET s.model         = $model,
            s.vfc2          = $vfc2,
            s.sentiment     = $sentiment,
            s.intensity     = $intensity,
            s.key_themes    = $key_themes,
            s.verbatim_samples = $verbatim,
            s.has_conflict  = $has_conflict,
            s.conflict_detail = $conflict_detail,
            s.data_gaps     = $data_gaps,
            s.evidence_tier = $tier,
            s.feedback_count = $count,
            s.ai_inferred_vfc = $ai_inferred

    """,

        sentiment=signal.get("sentiment", "neutral"),
        intensity=float(signal.get("intensity", 5.0)),
        key_themes=signal.get("key_themes", []),
        verbatim=signal.get("verbatim_samples", []),
        has_conflict=signal.get("has_conflict", False),
        conflict_detail=signal.get("conflict_detail"),
        data_gaps=signal.get("data_gaps", []),
        tier=tier,
        count=count,
        ai_inferred=signal.get("ai_inferred_vfc", False),
    )


def main():
    print("=== Step 04: Extract signals via Claude API ===")

    if LLM_PROVIDER == "openai":
        if not OPENAI_API_KEY:
            print("ERROR: OPENAI_API_KEY not set")
            sys.exit(1)
        client = llm_client_lib.OpenAI(api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY)
        print(f"  Using OpenAI model: {OPENAI_MODEL}")
    else:
        if not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:
            print("ERROR: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set")
            sys.exit(1)
        client = llm_client_lib.Anthropic(api_key=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
        print(f"  Using Anthropic model: {CLAUDE_MODEL}")
    driver = get_driver()

    with driver.session() as session:
        groups = load_feedback_by_vfc(session)
        print(f"  Found {len(groups)} (model, vfc2) groups")

        # Prepare batches
        items = [
            (model, vfc2, feedbacks)
            for (model, vfc2), feedbacks in groups.items()
            if len(feedbacks) >= MIN_FEEDBACKS
        ]
        print(f"  Processing {len(items)} groups (≥{MIN_FEEDBACKS} feedbacks)")

        total_signals = 0
        for batch_start in range(0, len(items), BATCH_SIZE):
            batch_items = items[batch_start: batch_start + BATCH_SIZE]
            batch_payload = [
                {
                    "model": model,
                    "vfc2": vfc2,
                    "feedback_count": len(feedbacks),
                    "feedbacks": [
                        {"text": fb["text"], "channel": fb["channel"], "ftype": fb["ftype"]}
                        for fb in feedbacks[:20]  # cap at 20 per group
                    ],
                }
                for model, vfc2, feedbacks in batch_items
            ]

            print(f"  Batch {batch_start // BATCH_SIZE + 1}: {len(batch_payload)} VFC groups...")
            try:
                signals = call_llm(client, batch_payload)
                for i, (model, vfc2, feedbacks) in enumerate(batch_items):
                    if i < len(signals):
                        save_signal(session, model, vfc2, signals[i], len(feedbacks))
                        total_signals += 1
                time.sleep(0.5)  # rate limit courtesy
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  [ERROR] Batch {batch_start // BATCH_SIZE + 1}: {e}")
                continue

        print(f"  Total signals saved: {total_signals}")

    driver.close()
    print("Done.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Step 05 — Correlate signals with customer study metrics.

For each Signal node, finds matching CustomerStudyMetric nodes (by VFC2 keyword
match or direct dimension mapping) and:
  - Creates CONTEXTUALIZES edges: study metric → signal
  - Updates signal confidence based on study alignment
  - Flags divergence: signal sentiment vs. study score direction

  - Signal WEAK + study score available → upgraded to MODERATE
  - Signal MODERATE + study aligns → upgraded to STRONG
  - Signal vs. study diverge >2pts on 10-pt scale → has_conflict = True

Run: python pipeline/05_correlate_studies.py
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
from config import NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD, MODELS_IN_SCOPE
from neo4j import GraphDatabase

# Manual VFC2 → study dimension/question keyword mappings
# (supplement the auto keyword-match from step 02)
VFC_TO_STUDY_KEYWORDS = {
    "INFOTAINMENT":        ["infotainment", "display", "screen", "iDrive", "multimedia"],
    "CONNECTIVITY":        ["connectivity", "bluetooth", "wifi", "wireless", "phone"],
    "NAVIGATION":          ["navigation", "maps", "GPS", "routing"],
    "COMFORT":             ["comfort", "seat", "interior", "cabin", "ergonomic"],
    "CHARGING":            ["charging", "charge", "range", "battery", "electric"],
    "DRIVING_DYNAMICS":    ["driving", "dynamics", "handling", "steering", "performance"],
    "SAFETY":              ["safety", "assist", "ADAS", "brake", "warning"],
    "EXTERIOR_DESIGN":     ["design", "exterior", "styling", "look"],
    "NOISE_VIBRATION":     ["noise", "vibration", "NVH", "quiet", "sound"],
    "CLIMATE_CONTROL":     ["climate", "air conditioning", "heating", "ventilation", "temperature"],
    "LIGHTING":            ["lighting", "light", "headlight", "ambient"],
    "VOICE_CONTROL":       ["voice", "assistant", "speech", "Alexa", "Hey BMW"],
    "OTA_UPDATES":         ["OTA", "update", "software", "firmware", "over-the-air"],
    "STORAGE_SPACE":       ["storage", "boot", "trunk", "space", "luggage"],
    "SUSPENSION":          ["suspension", "ride", "rough", "smooth"],
}

# Study score neutral midpoint on 1-10 scale
NEUTRAL_MIDPOINT = 5.5
DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD = 2.0  # pts on 1-10 scale


def get_driver():
    return GraphDatabase.driver(NEO4J_URI, auth=(NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD))


def load_signals(session) -> list[dict]:
    result = session.run("""
        MATCH (s:Signal)
        RETURN s.signal_id AS sid, s.model AS model, s.vfc2 AS vfc2,
               s.sentiment AS sentiment, s.evidence_tier AS tier,
               s.has_conflict AS has_conflict
    """)
    return [dict(row) for row in result]


def find_study_metrics(session, model: str, vfc2: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Find CustomerStudyMetric nodes matching this model and VFC2."""
    keywords = VFC_TO_STUDY_KEYWORDS.get(vfc2, [vfc2.lower().replace("_", " ")])
    matched = []

    for kw in keywords:
        result = session.run("""
            MATCH (s:CustomerStudyMetric)
            WHERE s.model = $model
              AND (
                toLower(coalesce(s.dimension, '')) CONTAINS toLower($kw)
                OR toLower(coalesce(s.question, '')) CONTAINS toLower($kw)
              )
            RETURN s.id AS sid, s.study AS study, s.score AS score,
                   coalesce(s.dimension, s.question) AS label
            LIMIT 3
        """, model=model, kw=kw)
        for row in result:
            entry = dict(row)
            if not any(m["sid"] == entry["sid"] for m in matched):
                matched.append(entry)

    return matched


def sentiment_to_direction(sentiment: str) -> float:
    """Convert sentiment to direction relative to neutral midpoint."""
    return {"positive": 1.0, "negative": -1.0, "neutral": 0.0}.get(sentiment, 0.0)


def study_score_direction(score: float) -> float:
    """Score above midpoint = positive signal, below = negative."""
    if score is None:
        return 0.0
    return 1.0 if score > NEUTRAL_MIDPOINT else (-1.0 if score < NEUTRAL_MIDPOINT else 0.0)


def upgrade_tier(current_tier: str, has_study: bool, aligned: bool) -> str:
    if not has_study:
        return current_tier
    if current_tier == "WEAK" and has_study:
        return "MODERATE"
    if current_tier == "MODERATE" and aligned:
        return "STRONG"
    return current_tier


def correlate_signal(session, signal: dict, study_metrics: list[dict]):
    if not study_metrics:
        return

    sid = signal["sid"]
    model = signal["model"]
    sentiment_dir = sentiment_to_direction(signal["sentiment"])

    has_conflict = signal.get("has_conflict", False)
    study_dirs = []
    avg_score = 0.0
    aligned = True

    for metric in study_metrics:
        score = metric.get("score")
        if score is None:
            continue
        avg_score += float(score)
        study_dir = study_score_direction(float(score))
        study_dirs.append(study_dir)

        diverges = (sentiment_dir != 0 and study_dir != 0
                    and sentiment_dir != study_dir
                    and abs(float(score) - NEUTRAL_MIDPOINT) > DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD)
        if diverges:
            aligned = False
            has_conflict = True

        # Link study metric → signal
        session.run("""
            MATCH (sig:Signal {signal_id: $sid})
            MATCH (sm:CustomerStudyMetric {id: $metric_id})
            MERGE (sm)-[:CONTEXTUALIZES]->(sig)
            SET sm.linked_signal = $sid
        """, sid=sid, metric_id=metric["sid"])

    if study_dirs:
        avg_score = avg_score / len(study_metrics)
        new_tier = upgrade_tier(signal["tier"], True, aligned)

        session.run("""
            MATCH (s:Signal {signal_id: $sid})
            SET s.study_avg_score    = $avg_score,
                s.study_aligned      = $aligned,
                s.has_conflict       = $has_conflict,
                s.evidence_tier      = $new_tier,
                s.study_metric_count = $count
        """, sid=sid, avg_score=round(avg_score, 3),
             aligned=aligned, has_conflict=has_conflict,
             new_tier=new_tier, count=len(study_dirs))


def main():
    print("=== Step 05: Correlate signals with customer studies ===")
    driver = get_driver()

    with driver.session() as session:
        signals = load_signals(session)
        print(f"  Processing {len(signals)} signals")

        upgraded  = 0
        linked    = 0
        conflicts = 0

        for sig in signals:
            metrics = find_study_metrics(session, sig["model"], sig["vfc2"])
            if not metrics:
                continue
            linked += 1

            old_tier = sig["tier"]
            correlate_signal(session, sig, metrics)

            # Re-read to check if upgraded
            row = session.run(
                "MATCH (s:Signal {signal_id:$sid}) RETURN s.evidence_tier AS t, s.has_conflict AS c",
                sid=sig["sid"],
            ).single()
            if row and row["t"] != old_tier:
                upgraded += 1
                print(f"    ↑ {sig['sid']} [{sig['model']}] {old_tier} → {row['t']}")
            if row and row["c"] and not sig.get("has_conflict"):
                conflicts += 1
                print(f"    ⚠ {sig['sid']} [{sig['model']}] study diverges from feedback sentiment")

        print(f"\n  Signals linked to study metrics: {linked}/{len(signals)}")
        print(f"  Evidence tier upgrades:          {upgraded}")
        print(f"  New conflicts detected:          {conflicts}")

    driver.close()
    print("Done.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Step 06 — Generate product requirements from signals using Claude API.

For each Signal with evidence_tier STRONG or MODERATE, Claude generates
a structured Requirement with:
  - JTBD format
  - BMW-style Metric Specification
  - SMART check
  - RICE + BMW Priority Score
  - Kano + MoSCoW
  - Decision Gate (GREEN/AMBER/RED)
  - Conflict and data gap surfacing

Run: python pipeline/06_generate_requirements.py
"""
import json
import sys
import time
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
from config import (
    NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD,
    OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL,
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_MODEL,
    LLM_PROVIDER, EVIDENCE_TIERS, BMW_PRIORITY_WEIGHTS,
    GATE_GREEN_MIN_CONFIDENCE, GATE_AMBER_MIN_CONFIDENCE,
    MARKET_REACH_BASE, SALES_VOLUMES,
)
from neo4j import GraphDatabase

if LLM_PROVIDER == "openai":
    import openai as llm_client_lib
else:
    import anthropic as llm_client_lib

BATCH_SIZE = 5


SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a BMW Senior Product Manager generating formal product requirements.

For each input signal, generate a structured requirement following BMW standards.
Output a JSON array — one object per signal.

Required schema:
{
  "req_id_suffix": "001",            // sequential, will be prefixed with model
  "title": "Charging Speed ≥150kW DC",
  "jtbd": "When I … I want … so that …",
  "metric_spec": {
    "current_value": "50kW (AC only)",
    "target_value": "≥150kW",
    "unit": "kW DC",
    "timeframe": "at launch (MY2027)"
  },
  "smart_check": {
    "specific": true,
    "measurable": true,
    "attainable": true,
    "relevant": true,
    "timely": true
  },
  "smart_notes": "Attainable: Tesla Model 3 LR achieves 250kW. Relevant: BEV target 50% by 2030.",
  "impact_score": 8.5,              // 0-10, based on signal intensity + feedback count
  "effort_estimate": 6,             // 1-10 story points, PM estimate
  "kano": "Must-Be",                // Must-Be / One-Dimensional / Attractive
  "moscow": "Must-Have",            // Must-Have / Should-Have / Could-Have / Won't-Have
  "rationale": "340 feedbacks (STRONG evidence). Competitor parity required (BMW Annual Report: BEV target 50% by 2030).",
  "data_gaps": ["No US market data for F70 (not sold there)", "No longitudinal study on charging satisfaction"],
  "notes": null
}

CRITICAL RULES:
1. JTBD must follow exact format: "When I [context], I want [action/feature], so that [outcome]."
2. metric_spec.target_value must be measurable with a unit (not vague: NOT 'better', NOT 'improved').
3. SMART attainable must reference competitor data or BMW capability — never guess.
4. impact_score must be justified by the signal intensity and feedback_count, not invented.
5. If has_conflict is true for the signal, moscow must be at most 'Should-Have' pending PM resolution.
6. If evidence_tier is WEAK, add a prominent data_gap: 'WEAK EVIDENCE: only N feedbacks. Confidence low.'
7. effort_estimate is a PM rough estimate — flag it as 'requires Engineering validation'."""


def get_driver():
    return GraphDatabase.driver(NEO4J_URI, auth=(NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD))


def load_signals(session) -> list[dict]:
    result = session.run("""
        MATCH (s:Signal)
        WHERE s.evidence_tier IN ['STRONG', 'MODERATE']
        RETURN s.signal_id AS sid,
               s.model AS model, s.vfc2 AS vfc2,
               s.sentiment AS sentiment, s.intensity AS intensity,
               s.key_themes AS themes, s.verbatim_samples AS verbatim,
               s.has_conflict AS has_conflict, s.conflict_detail AS conflict_detail,
               s.data_gaps AS data_gaps, s.evidence_tier AS tier,
               s.feedback_count AS count
        ORDER BY s.intensity DESC
    """)
    return [dict(row) for row in result]


def compute_rice(reach: int, impact: float, confidence: float, effort: float) -> float:
    return round((reach * impact * confidence) / max(effort, 1), 2)


def compute_bmw_priority(impact: float, market_reach_norm: float, effort: float) -> float:
    w = BMW_PRIORITY_WEIGHTS
    return round(
        w["impact"] * impact
        + w["market_reach"] * market_reach_norm
        + w["effort_inverse"] * (10 - effort),
        2,
    )


def determine_gate(evidence_tier: str, has_conflict: bool, confidence: float) -> str:
    if evidence_tier == "WEAK" or confidence < GATE_AMBER_MIN_CONFIDENCE:
        return "RED"
    if has_conflict or confidence < GATE_GREEN_MIN_CONFIDENCE:
        return "AMBER"

"""Pydantic models shared across pipeline and API."""
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Literal, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


# ── Enums / Literals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ModelCode       = Literal["F70", "G60", "G70"]
EvidenceTier    = Literal["STRONG", "MODERATE", "WEAK"]
GateColor       = Literal["GREEN", "AMBER", "RED"]
KanoType        = Literal["Must-Be", "One-Dimensional", "Attractive"]
MoSCoW          = Literal["Must-Have", "Should-Have", "Could-Have", "Won't-Have"]
RequirementStatus = Literal[
    "DRAFT", "PM_REVIEW", "APPROVED", "REJECTED", "POSTPONED", "CONFLICTED"
]
ActorRole       = Literal["AI_SYSTEM", "PM_USER", "ENG_LEAD"]


# ── Signal ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class Signal(BaseModel):
    signal_id:         str
    model:             ModelCode
    vfc2:              str
    vfc3:              Optional[str] = None
    sentiment:         Literal["positive", "negative", "neutral"]
    intensity:         float = Field(..., ge=0, le=10)
    feedback_count:    int
    source_channels:   list[str]
    evidence_tier:     EvidenceTier
    summary:           str
    verbatim_samples:  list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=3)
    has_conflict:      bool = False
    conflict_detail:   Optional[str] = None
    data_gaps:         list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


# ── Requirement ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class MetricSpec(BaseModel):
    """BMW-style metric: 'Cabin temp from 35°C to 22°C in ≤8 min'"""
    current_value:  Optional[str] = None
    target_value:   str
    unit:           str
    timeframe:      Optional[str] = None


class RequirementScore(BaseModel):
    impact:             float = Field(..., ge=0, le=10)
    market_reach_norm:  float = Field(..., ge=0, le=10)
    effort:             float = Field(..., ge=1, le=10)
    confidence:         float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
    reach_count:        int
    rice_score:         float
    bmw_priority:       float
    bmw_priority_low:   float   # confidence interval lower bound
    bmw_priority_high:  float   # confidence interval upper bound


class Requirement(BaseModel):
    req_id:           str                        # e.g. REQ-F70-001
    model:            ModelCode
    title:            str
    jtbd:             str                        # "When I … I want … so that …"
    metric_spec:      MetricSpec
    smart_check:      dict[str, bool]            # S/M/A/R/T
    score:            RequirementScore
    kano:             KanoType
    moscow:           MoSCoW
    evidence_tier:    EvidenceTier
    gate_color:       GateColor
    status:           RequirementStatus = "DRAFT"
    source_signals:   list[str]                  # signal_ids
    vfc_tags:         list[str]
    data_gaps:        list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    conflict_detail:  Optional[str] = None
    notes:            Optional[str] = None


# ── Requirement status transition ──────────────────────────────────────────
class StatusTransition(BaseModel):
    req_id:        str
    to_status:     RequirementStatus
    actor:         str
    actor_role:    ActorRole
    rationale:     Optional[str] = None          # required for REJECTED/POSTPONED
    score_override: Optional[float] = None       # if PM overrides BMW Priority


# ── Audit event ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class AuditEvent(BaseModel):
    entity_id:    str
    entity_type:  str
    action:       str
    actor:        str
    actor_role:   ActorRole
    timestamp:    str
    payload_hash: str
    detail:       Optional[str] = None

"""Pydantic models shared across pipeline and API."""
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Literal, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


# ── Enums / Literals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ModelCode       = Literal["F70", "G60", "G70"]
EvidenceTier    = Literal["STRONG", "MODERATE", "WEAK"]
GateColor       = Literal["GREEN", "AMBER", "RED"]
KanoType        = Literal["Must-Be", "One-Dimensional", "Attractive"]
MoSCoW          = Literal["Must-Have", "Should-Have", "Could-Have", "Won't-Have"]
RequirementStatus = Literal[
    "DRAFT", "PM_REVIEW", "APPROVED", "REJECTED", "POSTPONED", "CONFLICTED"
]
ActorRole       = Literal["AI_SYSTEM", "PM_USER", "ENG_LEAD"]


# ── Signal ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class Signal(BaseModel):
    signal_id:         str
    model:             ModelCode
    vfc2:              str
    vfc3:              Optional[str] = None
    sentiment:         Literal["positive", "negative", "neutral"]
    intensity:         float = Field(..., ge=0, le=10)
    feedback_count:    int
    source_channels:   list[str]
    evidence_tier:     EvidenceTier
    summary:           str
    verbatim_samples:  list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=3)
    has_conflict:      bool = False
    conflict_detail:   Optional[str] = None
    data_gaps:         list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


# ── Requirement ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class MetricSpec(BaseModel):
    """BMW-style metric: 'Cabin temp from 35°C to 22°C in ≤8 min'"""
    current_value:  Optional[str] = None
    target_value:   str
    unit:           str
    timeframe:      Optional[str] = None


class RequirementScore(BaseModel):
    impact:             float = Field(..., ge=0, le=10)
    market_reach_norm:  float = Field(..., ge=0, le=10)
    effort:             float = Field(..., ge=1, le=10)
    confidence:         float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
    reach_count:        int
    rice_score:         float
    bmw_priority:       float
    bmw_priority_low:   float   # confidence interval lower bound
    bmw_priority_high:  float   # confidence interval upper bound


class Requirement(BaseModel):
    req_id:           str                        # e.g. REQ-F70-001
    model:            ModelCode
    title:            str
    jtbd:             str                        # "When I … I want … so that …"
    metric_spec:      MetricSpec
    smart_check:      dict[str, bool]            # S/M/A/R/T
    score:            RequirementScore
    kano:             KanoType
    moscow:           MoSCoW
    evidence_tier:    EvidenceTier
    gate_color:       GateColor
    status:           RequirementStatus = "DRAFT"
    source_signals:   list[str]                  # signal_ids
    vfc_tags:         list[str]
    data_gaps:        list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    conflict_detail:  Optional[str] = None
    notes:            Optional[str] = None


# ── Requirement status transition ──────────────────────────────────────────
class StatusTransition(BaseModel):
    req_id:        str
    to_status:     RequirementStatus
    actor:         str
    actor_role:    ActorRole
    rationale:     Optional[str] = None          # required for REJECTED/POSTPONED
    score_override: Optional[float] = None       # if PM overrides BMW Priority


# ── Audit event ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class AuditEvent(BaseModel):
    entity_id:    str
    entity_type:  str
    action:       str
    actor:        str
    actor_role:   ActorRole
    timestamp:    str
    payload_hash: str
    detail:       Optional[str] = None

### 8.4 Events and Reconstructability

Record these event categories:

| Event | What must be reconstructable |
| :--- | :--- |
| `SOURCE_IMPORTED` | File version, parser/mapping version, row counts, exclusions/errors |
| `SIGNAL_CONSOLIDATED` / `SIGNAL_REVISED` | Membership, consolidation method, counts, source scope, before/after signal snapshots |
| `REQUIREMENT_DERIVED` | Signal/source versions, retrieved evidence, run/model/prompt references, initial content |
| `CONTENT_CHANGED` / `EVIDENCE_CHANGED` | Previous/new revision and exact field/evidence changes |
| `SCORE_CALCULATED` / `SCORE_OVERRIDDEN` | Inputs, formula/config, factor contributions, original/effective score, rationale |
| `RANKING_RECALCULATED` | Previous/new baseline ID-to-rank map, scores, context, trigger; visible moves for affected requirements |
| `STATUS_CHANGED` | Actor, previous/new status, approved revision, decision rationale |
| `CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` / `CHALLENGE_COMPLETED` | PM question, cited response, proposed diff, application state |
| `SUGGESTION_APPLIED` / `SUGGESTION_DISCARDED` | Turn/run reference, proposed versus accepted patch, PM rationale, resulting revision or no-op outcome |
| `FREEZE_CREATED` | Approved revisions, source/config versions, accepted assumptions, actor, checkpoint |

Every event has UTC time, initiator kind/ID, entity/version, and a non-empty human or generated rationale. Store model output/context references locally for AI derivations; generation is not claimed to be mathematically deterministic.

Audit view combines requirement events with its linked signal/run/source events so the PM can follow the complete chain. Ranking history uses the baseline full-list context; sorting/filtering a table changes only the view and is not a governance event.

For tamper evidence, hash canonical event JSON plus the previous event hash. Provide a verifier and include the checkpoint in the exported package. This is a tamper-evident local ledger relative to a trusted checkpoint, not a claim that a database administrator cannot rewrite history.

## 9. API and Frontend Contracts

### 9.1 API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose / payload |
| :--- | :--- |
| `GET /api/sources` | Import state, file hashes, row/comment counts, parsing issues |
| `GET /api/sources/{id}` | Source file metadata and import state |
| `GET /api/source-records/{id}` | Exact workbook row/cell or extracted fact with original locator |
| `GET /api/document-chunks/{id}` | Exact cited PDF text and page metadata |
| `GET /api/sources/{id}/file` | Allowlisted imported PDF download/view |
| `POST /api/import-runs` | Import the configured local BMW dataset; returns an analysis-compatible run ID |
| `POST /api/analysis-runs` | Requested scope, selected signals/topics, max drafts, refresh/cache option; returns run ID |
| `GET /api/analysis-runs/{id}` | State/stage, progress, failures, model/cache mode, resulting requirement IDs |
| `GET /api/signals` | Consolidated findings with scope, distinct counts, and evidence links |
| `POST /api/review-threads` | Bind a contextual conversation to a signal or requirement ID |
| `GET /api/review-threads/{id}` | Visible turns, citations, suggestion states, and current entity revision |
| `POST /api/review-threads/{id}/turns` | Question, expected entity revision, actor, rationale; returns a challenge run ID |
| `POST /api/review-threads/{id}/turns/{turn_id}/discard` | Mark a pending suggestion discarded, actor and rationale; no requirement mutation |
| `GET /api/requirements` | Paginated/searchable table; derivative, region, powertrain, status, evidence filters |
| `GET /api/requirements/{id}` | Complete current revision, score, uncertainty, and decision controls |
| `GET /api/requirements/{id}/evidence` | Supporting/opposing/context evidence, locators, facts, regional coverage |
| `PATCH /api/requirements/{id}` | SMART/scope/evidence/factor edits plus expected revision, actor, rationale |
| `POST /api/requirements/{id}/decisions` | Start review, approve, reject, defer, or reopen; expected revision and rationale |
| `POST /api/requirements/{id}/challenges` | Convenience wrapper creating/reusing a requirement thread and submitting a turn; returns run ID |
| `POST /api/requirements/{id}/challenge-applications` | Turn/run reference, expected revision, accepted allowed diff, actor, rationale; apply one proposal once |
| `GET /api/requirements/{id}/history` | Revision diffs and linked consolidation/scoring/ranking/decision events |
| `GET /api/requirements/{id}/history/export?format=json` | Download the reconstructable requirement history and referenced context |
| `GET /api/requirements/export?format=csv\|json` | Structured sample list, including linked evidence, score rationale, ECI, assumptions, status |
| `POST /api/freezes` | Selected requirement IDs/revisions, expected baseline ranking ID, actor, rationale |
| `GET /api/freezes/{id}` | Immutable review-package snapshot |
| `GET /api/freezes/{id}/export?format=markdown\|json` | G1 package from the stored snapshot |
| `GET /api/freezes/{id}/audit` | Audit bundle with revision/tool references and complete chain prefix through the snapshot checkpoint |
| `POST /api/scoring/preview` | Optional sensitivity preview; no baseline writes |

Register the static `/api/requirements/export` route before the `/{id}` route. Run polling uses a common response shape for import, analysis, and challenge jobs.

All contextual chat uses the same review service. The convenience challenge route is an adapter, not a second implementation. Applying a proposal is idempotent by turn ID; an identical repeat request returns the original application result rather than creating another revision. A conflicting reapplication returns 409. Record the application result and requirement mutation in the same transaction.

Example approval request:

```json
{
  "action": "approve",
  "expected_revision": 3,
  "actor_id": "pm-demo-1",
  "actor_role": "PM_USER",
  "rationale": "Reviewed linked evidence and accepted the proposed usability target for concept planning.",
  "reviewed_target_ids": ["metric-1", "milestone-1"],
  "accepted_assumption_ids": ["assumption-1"]
}
```

The server determines the new revision, status, timestamp, score, and events. The client cannot submit a fabricated approval state or final calculated score.

### 9.2 Main Screen

Header: dataset/run state, **Run analysis**, **Export sample list**, **Create review package**.

Filters: source/target derivative, region, powertrain, status, evidence level, text search.

Table columns: rank, ID/title, target scope, effective priority, evidence level, uncertainty/conflict badges, status. Row selection opens the workbench. Empty, failed, partial, and cached states are explicit.

### 9.3 Workbench

Use tabs or sections within one large drawer/panel:

- **Requirement:** problem, description, editable SMART fields, target provenance, alternatives, assumptions.
- **Why this priority:** four factor values, weighted contributions, input references, provisional range, override controls, generated score rationale.
- **Evidence:** verbatim spans, source/type, worksheet/cell/page link, support/opposition label, bucket-versus-issue counts, regional coverage and survey context.
- **Review assistant:** scoped conversation, clickable citations, visible retrieval progress, coverage gaps, and a change-preview card with Apply/Edit/Discard controls. Applying and approving are separate buttons/actions.
- **History:** chronological events and revision diff, including score/rank/status moves.

Persistent actions: **Start review**, **Edit**, **Challenge**, **Approve**, **Reject**, **Defer**. A decision dialog requires rationale and shows outstanding targets/assumptions. Invalid actions are disabled and server-enforced.

After a confirmed mutation, refresh server detail/list/history/ranking and invalidate matching Streamlit cache/session data. Preserve unsaved editor state if an API request fails. Show a reload/compare prompt for HTTP 409. Rendering/rerunning the UI must not itself submit mutations.

Owner 4 reads explicit API_BASE_URL instead of hard-coded localhost, normalizes legacy `gate` list versus `gate_color` detail fields, and shows score policy/scale. An override-enabled control distinguishes zero from disabled. Empty legacy histories, unresolved citations and model SMART flags have accurate validation labels; GREEN is an evidence/gate display, not PM approval. Empty API results remain distinct from failures.

### 9.4 Sources and Review Package Screens

The sources screen shows actual imported counts, source errors, region/powertrain coverage, and source previews. The review-package screen shows selected approved revisions, unresolved-but-accepted assumptions, baseline scores, and snapshot/download controls.

Keep the BMW-inspired styling consistent: navy `#061a38`, blue `#1c69d4`, neutral slate, amber for uncertainty. Prioritize legible evidence and review controls over decorative charts.

## 10. Export Behavior

### 10.1 Structured Sample List

CSV/JSON export includes ID, revision, description/SMART fields, linked finding/source identifiers and locators, score and factor breakdown, prioritization rationale, evidence index/level, future assumptions, uncertainties, and decision status.

JSON retains nested structures. CSV flattens the main fields and serializes evidence/assumption arrays predictably; it must not silently omit them.

Generate complete exports server-side, independent of table pagination/limit. The reviewed UI downloads summary rows capped at 200 despite 250 proposals; the reviewed CSV omits linked sources/gaps/assumptions. A 250-record fixture must export all 250 with the full BMW field set. Frontend requests that endpoint rather than building files from its displayed page.

### 10.2 Frozen G1 Package

`POST /api/freezes` validates that each supplied revision is current and approved and that the baseline ranking context has not changed. It captures full requirement payloads, score/configuration, source/signal versions, decisions, accepted assumptions, and an audit checkpoint in one transaction.

Generate Markdown and JSON from that stored snapshot. Later edits to a requirement do not change an existing package. PDF can be added using browser print after the core exports work.

The Markdown package contains an executive summary, prioritized approved list, SMART descriptions, source references, scoring rationale, confidence/coverage, open validations, and decision history. Include a machine-readable manifest and checkpoint for verification.

### 10.3 Audit Export

Provide `GET /api/freezes/{id}/audit` and a JSON download on the history view. For a freeze, export the relevant chronological source/run/signal/requirement/ranking events, revision snapshots, and visible tool/assistant records needed to reconstruct each selected decision.

Hash-chain verification requires the complete event prefix through the stored checkpoint, or an explicit proof linking omitted events. The core build exports the complete prefix plus selected-requirement references so a verifier does not mistake a filtered event list for a complete chain. Write `audit.json` and the manifest beside the review package in the private export bundle.

Owner 3 coordinates root `models.py`/`config.py`, constraints, dependencies, API entry points and runner/Compose. ### 11.2 Independent Work and Handoffs

## 12. Verification and Demonstration

### 12.1 Meaningful Checks

- **Import correctness:** expected raw/distinct counts; repeated-ID annotations survive; mixed positive/negative comments remain multi-topic; rerunning the same import is idempotent.
- **Provenance:** sampled comments, survey cells, volume facts, and cited PDF passages match the actual source. All generated citation IDs resolve.
- **Signal counts:** duplicate annotations and multiple spans do not inflate distinct-comment support; broad bucket counts cannot become narrow-issue counts.
- **Scoring:** factors stay bounded, weights sum to one, missing inputs remain provisional, same inputs/config reproduce scores, volume keys are not double-counted, complexity importance affects scores as specified.
- **Workflow:** AI cannot approve; a blank rationale fails; stale revision fails; editing an approved requirement invalidates approval; failed writes cannot leave an unlogged state change.
- **Review assistant:** retrieval uses real identifiers; read-only chat/discard cannot mutate requirements; pending edits have validated score previews; applying once creates one revision; stale suggestions cannot overwrite newer work; applying never implicitly approves.
- **History:** derivation, consolidation, evidence edits, factor/score changes, resulting rank moves, and PM decisions are reconstructable with actors/times/reasons.
- **Freeze:** unapproved/stale revisions cannot be frozen; changing the live requirement does not change an existing package; all required sample-list fields survive export.
- **Recovery:** cached/live runs are distinguished, partial failures display, saved decisions/history survive restart, and changed audit events fail verification against the trusted checkpoint.

| Gate | Required proof | Owners |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Baseline/contracts, first 45 minutes** | Reviewed code integrated deliberately; shared model/step-06 ownership agreed; tested environment/paths/provider selection and API payloads documented | 3 coordinates 1/2/4 |
| **One trustworthy vertical slice, target hour 3** | Real original IDs/spans; keyed valid generation; score policy labeled; guarded PM decision and atomic history; UI opens without mutation | 1/2/3/4, witnessed by 5 |
| **Source/sample readiness, target hour 6** | Native study/G68/sales/strategy/equipment evidence; quote reconciliation for every showcase claim; complete field contract and source/target assumptions | 1/2/3 |
| **Decision/export readiness, target hour 8** | Reruns preserve decisions; apply and approve separate; complete exports/history/freeze; source gaps/weak case visible | 2/3/4 |
| **Judged demonstration, hours 8–10** | All P0 repair proofs; real Neo4j rollback/query checks, actual container networking, raw conversion and cited live model run; three verified cases, honest cache/fixture labels and private artifact bundle | 3 coordinates all; 5 rehearses/checks |

For regression tests, use the recorded counterexamples: AI_SYSTEM approval with no rationale; conflicting route/body IDs; override 999; audit failure after status write; same-prefix signal names; reversed model output; rerun over approved data; G68_CN/native distribution; WEAK plus opposing study; and a 250-record export. Preserve the distinction between synthetic/mocked proof and real graph/container/source/model checks.

The reviewed export's 218 SMART-true flags, 225 empty-gap arrays and 538 text matches are not acceptance evidence by themselves. Showcase requirements need independently resolved sources/assignment, reviewed target provenance and a real chronological decision history.

### 12.2 Three Showcase Cases

Select cases after inspecting actual evidence; do not hard-code assumed complaint counts or regional preferences.

1. **Strong support:** recurring issue with valid quotes and relevant corroboration.
2. **Trade-off:** a genuine conflict or two plausible solutions with traceable evidence and effort differences.
3. **Evidence gap:** a valuable successor/regional proposal whose applicability or target needs validation.

The demonstration follows one case through drafting, score explanation, original evidence, PM modification, approval, history, and export. The other two show why uncertainty and trade-offs are useful decision outputs.

### 12.3 Definition of Done

- [ ] Prototype imports the supplied heterogeneous data and exposes actual import/coverage state.
- [ ] A new proposed requirement can be generated from real findings in the app.
- [ ] The structured sample list contains every BMW-required field and exports successfully.
- [ ] Every requirement has traceable findings/sources and a reproducible score rationale.
- [ ] Proposed targets, future assumptions, evidence gaps, and conflicts are visible.
- [ ] PM edit, challenge, approve, reject, and defer work with revisions and rationale.
- [ ] Contextual chat retrieves cited evidence and presents changes that a PM explicitly applies, edits, or discards before a separate approval.
- [ ] Audit history traces sources → consolidation → requirement → score/rank → human decision.
- [ ] Relevant content, evidence, score, priority, and status changes record initiator, timestamp, and rationale.
- [ ] Approved revisions can be frozen/exported without later edits altering the snapshot.
- [ ] Three verified examples and a rehearsed 3–5 minute pitch demonstrate the complete core loop.

**Measure the prototype's actual contribution:** time to first cited draft, time to review a requirement, and traceability coverage. Present acceleration of these activities rather than claiming the entire two-year development process has been eliminated.
